units: <cite ref="Yevamot 80b:5">Yeb. 80ᵇ</cite> <he>עושה כ׳</he> forms a bow (when urinating).
<cite ref="Yoma 11b:5">Yoma 11ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Eruvin 11b:14">Erub. 11ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ ר״מ וכ׳</he> as to an arched doorway R. M. says, it requires a M’zuzah.

<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 7:2">Tosef. ib. VII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Eiruvin 5:2">V</cite>), 2 <he>עד מקום הכי׳</he> (ed. Zuck. <he>הקופא</he>) to the site of the (now ruined) arch (of Tiberias); Y. ib. V, 22ᵈ bot. <he>עד הכ׳</he>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nazir 7:1:9">Y. Naz. VII, 56ᵃ</cite> top <he>הגיעו לכ׳</he> when they arrived at the arch (or arcade).
<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 1:7">Ab. Zar. I, 7</cite> (<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 16a:13">16ᵃ</cite>) <he>כ׳ שמעמידין וכ׳</he> the arched chamber in the bath where they put up idolatrous statues.

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 41:1">Pesik. R. s. 41</cite> <he>כ׳ של חשבונות … אותה כ׳</he> an arcade named Arch of Accounts (a sort of Exchange) existed outside of Jerusalem, and they used to go out and settle their accounts under this arcade &c. Tanḥ.
<cite ref="Exodus 17">B’shall. 17</cite> (ref. to <he>קפאו</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 15:8">Ex. XV, 8</cite>) <he>כמין כפה</he> (Mekh.
ib., Shir. s. 6 קופה) like a vault; a. e.—Esp. כִּיפַּת הרקיע, or כִּופָּה the heavenly arch, sky (believed to be a solid mass).
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 48">Gen. R. s. 48</cite>, beg.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 4:5">Gen. R. s. 4</cite> <he>הרקיע … ולמעלה … כ׳ וכ׳</he> the firmament is like a lake, and above the lake is the arch, and owing to the heat of the lake the arch exudes drops &c.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 25b:1">B. Bath. 25ᵇ</cite> <he>אחורי כ׳</he> back of (above) the sky.
<cite ref="Megillah 11a">Meg. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>ג׳ מלכו תחת הכ׳</he> Ms. M. 2 (ed. <he>בכ׳</he>, Ms. M. 1 <he>בקופה</he>) three persons ruled over the whole world; a. e.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 9:3">Snh. IX, 3</cite> <he>כונסין אותן לכ׳</he> they put them in prison (for life).
<cite ref="Mishnah Sanhedrin 9:5">Ib. 5</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:4:5">Y. Gitt. IV, 45ᵈ</cite> bot.; Bab.
<cite ref="Gittin 20a">Gitt. 20ᵃ</cite>; v. <cite ref="A02118"><he>אנדכתרי</he></cite>; Treat. ʿĂbadim ch. III (ed. Kirchh.) <he>קיפה</he>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 57b:2">Sabb. 57ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ של צמר</he> a woolen cap, v. <cite ref="K00041"><he>כָּבוּל</he> II</cite>. Y. ib. V, end, 7ᶜ <he>כ׳ של צמר</he> a woolen cap on the head of a lamb, v. <cite ref="H01264"><he>חָנוּן</he> I</cite>; a. e.—
<cite ref="Tosefta Mikvaot 4:5">Tosef. Mikv. IV, 5</cite>, v. infra.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 10:1:15">Y. Snh. X, 27ᵈ</cite> bot.; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 3:7:15">Y. M. Kat. III, 83ᶜ</cite> top <he>כ׳ של אבנים</he> a heap of stones; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 100">Gen. R. s. 100</cite> <he>כִּיפַּת אבנים</he>.

<cite ref="Chullin 129a:7">Ḥull. 129ᵃ</cite> <he>כִּיפַּת שאור וכ׳</he> a heap (lump) of leavened dough which one intended to use as a block to sit on; <cite ref="Pesachim 45b">Pes. 45ᵇ</cite> <cite ref="K00357"><he>כופת</he></cite> some ed. (corr. acc.; Ms. M. 2 <cite ref="K00876"><he>כי׳</he></cite>; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 90); v. <cite ref="K00357"><he>כּוֹפֶת</he></cite>.—Pl. <cite ref="K00572"><he>כִּיפִּין</he></cite>, <he>כִּפִּים</he> (or <he>כֵּיפִ׳</he> fr. <cite ref="K00598"><he>כֵּיף</he></cite>)

<cite ref="Tosefta Shevi'it 7:16">Tosef. Shebi., VII, 16</cite> <he>על</he> (<he>של</he>) <he>בין הכֵּיפִ׳</he> ed. Zuck. (Var. <he>על מה שבכי׳</he>, <he>שבכופין</he>); <cite ref="Pesachim 53a:6">Pes. 53ᵃ</cite> <he>על של בין הכ׳</he> as long as there are fruits in the tops.

<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 2:1">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. II, 1</cite> <he>שכיפת שתי כ׳ של תמרה וכ׳</he> (R. S. to <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 22:9">Kel. XXII, 9</cite> <he>כופות</he>) who tied together two palm branches and sat upon them.

<cite ref="Mishnah Shabbat 24:2">Sabb. XXIV, 2</cite> <he>מפספסין את הכ׳</he> you may spread the bunches of branches (for fodder), contrad. to <cite ref="G00370"><he>זִירִין</he></cite> a. <cite ref="Q01492"><he>פְּקִיעִין</he></cite>.
Ib. 155ᵃ כ׳ תלתא bunches are called kippin when tied with three bands.—
